title: Evaluation Playbook + A/B Experiments — Horizon Retail
summary: Redwood demo of Evaluation Playbook: prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B experiments and quality gates. Horizon clarified success criteria (precision on product categorization, <200ms p95 for UX paths), data residency and SOC2 compliance requirement. Agreed next steps: send pilot pricing, share evaluation prompts + baseline benchmark, schedule 1-week POC kickoff.
action_items: Priya Nair: share Horizon-specific prompt template + sample eval deck (due 2026-11-04)
Jordan Lee: send pilot pricing + contract checklist (due 2026-11-05)
Carlos Mendez: provide 1 week of sample queries and SSO contact (due 2026-11-06)
next_steps: Share benchmark sheet link and baseline run (Redwood)
Customer to decide hosted vs Dedicated by end of week
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-02 16:00 PT | Duration: 46 minutes | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Horizon), Aisha Khan (Horizon), Tom Reeves (Horizon)

Auto-summary (AI): demo of Redwood Evaluate/Optimize features: prompt set versioning, regression alerts, A/B compare flows, and quality gates for production. Discussed SSO, SOC2, VPC, latency targets and pilot scope.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood. Priya is our SE and she'll walk through the evaluation playbook and the console. Carlos, Aisha, Tom, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: yeah thanks, Jordan. quick note, we have a hard cut of 45 minutes—got a meeting after—so if we could keep it tight that'd be great.
[00:20] Priya Nair: totally. i'll aim for a 30-minute walkthrough and 15 for Q&A, cool.
[00:26] Aisha Khan: sounds good. to kick off, our main ask — product categorization model drifting. we need a way to detect regressions from prompt/template changes and run A/B tests in prod without blinding the UX.
[00:39] Jordan Lee: perfect, that's exactly why we built the evaluation playbook. Priya, can you share screen?
[00:45] [screen share starts]
[00:48] Priya Nair: ok sharing now. so first slide is the playbook view — you can create 'prompt sets' which are versions of prompts tied to expected labels and metadata. you can attach golden examples and metrics to each set.
[01:05] Tom Reeves: is that the same as a dataset? or is it more like a test harness?
[01:10] Priya Nair: good question. it's more like a test harness — small curated prompt sets for targeted regression checks. you can import a CSV of examples or point to an S3 bucket for larger evals.
[01:21] Carlos Mendez: S3 is fine, but we need to keep data in our region. how does Redwood handle data residency with hosted API? we can't send PII out of EU.
[01:31] Jordan Lee: we have region controls on hosted infra. for EU-only data you can pin to eu-west-1; for stricter needs we support Redwood Private in a VPC or on-prem. both options integrate with KMS for key management.
[01:43] Aisha Khan: and SOC2? auditors will ask.
[01:46] Priya Nair: yes, SOC 2 Type II and ISO-whatever are listed in our security pack. we'll share the security whitepaper after this call.
[01:55] Carlos Mendez: cool. show us the actual alerts flow.
[01:58] Priya Nair: moving to the console — here's a sample project for retail categorization. you can see two prompt sets: baseline-v1 and candidate-v2. we run scheduled backfills and register metrics like exact match, top-k coverage, and a custom business metric: category-harm.
[02:18] [02:20] Speaker 4: can you annotate the custom metric?
[02:22] Priya Nair: sure. category-harm weights false positives on high-value categories heavier. you can author metrics in the UI or upload a small JS hook for custom scoring.
[02:33] Tom Reeves: how deterministic are metric runs? we need reproducible comparisons for legal/regulatory reasons.
[02:38] Priya Nair: all runs are versioned. every evaluation stores the prompt set id, model id (and model flags like quantization), dataset snapshot, and runtime artifact. you can export the exact configuration for audit.
[02:51] Carlos Mendez: that helps. latency — our UX path needs <200ms p95. do these evaluation runs emulate p95 latencies?
[03:00] Priya Nair: the evaluation runner has two modes: offline metrics and synthetic latency probes. for offline we run accuracy/quality metrics; for latency we have an integrated benchmark harness that will run against hosted endpoints or your dedicated pool to give you p50/p95 numbers.
[03:17] Jordan Lee: note that the benchmark harness also captures cost per 1k tokens so you can trade-off quantization or batching settings.
[03:26] Aisha Khan: on that tradeoff — if we quantize to 4-bit, do we see drops in exact match? we've seen this with other vendors.
[03:34] Priya Nair: it depends on the model and the class of queries. in the console, you can create A/B experiments where candidate gets a quantized variant and baseline is full-precision. the A/B compare shows per-slice regressions and a confidence interval.
[03:48] [03:50] Carlos Mendez: do you support automatic rollback for when a candidate crosses a regression threshold?
[03:56] Priya Nair: yes, through quality gates. you set thresholds on critical metrics; if candidate breaches, the routing policy will fall back to baseline automatically. we also support canary rollouts so only X% of traffic hits candidate.
[04:08] Tom Reeves: can we route by user segment? we have premium customers and beta cohorts.
[04:13] Priya Nair: absolutely — routing supports metadata-based routing, region, and account tier. you can do 10% traffic for beta accounts, for example.
[04:20] Aisha Khan: what's the simplest path to get started — hosted quick test or spin up dedicated?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: for evaluation we usually recommend hosted with pinned region for speed of onboarding. if you like the results and need isolation or sustained throughput we move to Dedicated. for strict compliance or air-gapped, Redwood Private.
[04:38] Carlos Mendez: budget-wise, hosted could be noisy. do you have cost estimates for a 1-week baseline for our size?
[04:45] Jordan Lee: we can estimate if you share query volume. rough ballpark: for a 1-week eval at 5M tokens/day, with evaluation runs plus latency probes, you'd likely be in the low thousands of dollars on hosted; Dedicated pricing is higher upfront but reduces unit costs. i'll send a detailed pilot quote.
[05:02] Aisha Khan: thanks. show us an A/B compare example — like output diffs with annotations.
[05:10] Priya Nair: switching to the A/B demo screen. here we have side-by-side outputs, pairwise scoring, and an integrated human-in-the-loop tool. you can label pairs and feed that back to the metric so over time your quality metric improves.
[05:28] [05:30] Carlos Mendez: is that annotation stored in our account or does Redwood store it? privacy again.
[05:35] Priya Nair: annotations and labels are stored in your account namespace. for hosted we encrypt at rest and use your KMS if you opt in. for Private, data never leaves your VPC.
[05:46] Tom Reeves: how often do regression alerts fire? we don't want alert fatigue.
[05:50] Priya Nair: alerts are configurable — there's a baseline hysteresis and grouping by slice. you can set a weekly summary and critical immediate alerts only if metric delta exceeds threshold and sustained for N runs.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: one customer turned on slice-level alerts and reduced noisy alerts by 70% by grouping small slices into umbrella categories.
[06:14] Aisha Khan: cool. can we test with our real traffic without exposing customers? maybe replay only.
[06:19] Priya Nair: yes, we support traffic replay into a test pool or run a shadow mode where the candidate gets no real user-facing exposure but we still gather metrics.
[06:29] Carlos Mendez: can Shadow mode simulate p95? we worry production is bursty.
[06:34] Priya Nair: shadow mode plus synthetic load generator gives you realistic p95 under expected concurrency. for more fidelity you can run the harness against your Dedicated pool.
[06:45] Tom Reeves: about integrations — do you integrate with our observability stack? we use Datadog and internal tracing.
[06:51] Priya Nair: yes, Redwood Console emits traces and metrics to Datadog, plus you can hook our tracing SDK to your request pipeline. we also provide exportable CSV/JSON for offline analysis.
[07:03] [07:05] Speaker 5: demo the regression alert detail and explain an example
[07:07] Priya Nair: sure — here's a regression alert triggered on 'category-harm' where candidate-v2 dropped 6% on premium categories. the alert page shows affected prompt sets, example pairs, and a suggested rollback. you can click to open the A/B comparison and escalate to engineering.
[07:24] Carlos Mendez: how is statistical significance determined? our legal wants to see confidence intervals.
[07:29] Priya Nair: we run bootstrap sampling for small datasets and asymptotic tests for larger ones; p-values and CIs are shown per-metric. you can export the test artifacts for audit.
[07:42] Aisha Khan: could we get a quick live A/B with one of our sample prompts? we shared a small CSV before the call — did you ingest it?
[07:51] Jordan Lee: Priya, did we load Horizon's sample?
[07:54] Priya Nair: yes, I pulled the CSV earlier — it's under 'Horizon sample set'. switching to live compare... loading...
[08:06] [08:10] Priya Nair: ok running baseline-v1 vs candidate-v2. showing a small slice: 'home electronics' prompt cluster. here's the pairwise diff — baseline returns category A, candidate returns category B for 3 of 20 examples.
[08:23] Tom Reeves: hm, candidate seems more generic. what's the model variant?
[08:27] Priya Nair: candidate is the same model but with a slightly different system prompt and a quantized runtime flag.
[08:34] Carlos Mendez: can we see the exact prompts and the token usage?
[08:38] Priya Nair: yes, expand details — here's prompt text, tokens consumed, and the full response.
[08:45] [08:46] Speaker 1: there's a slight transcription glitch — system prompt shows 'cate gory' split but it's UI only.
[08:51] Priya Nair: thanks, we'll note that. back to the run — you can tag any pair as 'false positive' and that will feed into a reweighting rule for future runs.
[09:01] Carlos Mendez: nice. i like the human-in-loop feedback. will that update live thresholds?
[09:06] Priya Nair: you can choose automatic threshold updates or manual review. many customers prefer manual review for first few cycles.
[09:15] Aisha Khan: about security docs — can you drop the SOC2 and VPC architecture links in the chat?
[09:20] Jordan Lee: yes i'll share. link to security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 and architecture whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/docs/private-vpc. also here's the evaluation deck we used: https://redwood.app/decks/horizon-eval-deck and benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/horizon-bench.xlsx
[09:41] Tom Reeves: looking ahead, what's the expected uplift we should expect from using Redwood Evaluate? any ROI examples?
[09:48] Priya Nair: varies by use case. one retail customer reduced manual triage by 40% and caught a model regression that would have impacted premium revenue by 2% of monthly run rate. the key is early detection and automated rollback.
[10:05] [10:07] Carlos Mendez: on the rollback — is there a delay window? we need a cooldown so we don't oscillate.
[10:12] Priya Nair: yes you set cooldown windows, and rollback actions are batched — there's also a dry-run mode so you can simulate rollback.
[10:21] Aisha Khan: what's the onboarding time for a pilot? three engineers on our side can dedicate 2 days next week.
[10:28] Jordan Lee: typical pilot onboarding is 2-4 business days to wire SSO, S3 access and seed the prompt sets; then 1 week of baseline runs. Priya will run the initial eval and show results in the second week.
[10:40] Tom Reeves: SSO — we run Okta.
[10:43] Priya Nair: Okta SAML is supported; we'll send the SSO setup doc.
[10:48] Carlos Mendez: any blockers with our infra? we use private subnet egress restrictions.
[10:53] Jordan Lee: for hosted, you'll need to open egress to the Redwood endpoints or use a Private Connect peering; for Private we deploy into your VPC. we'll map options after the call.
[11:05] [11:07] Speaker 2: can you show the alert tuning UI again?
[11:10] Priya Nair: sure — going back. here's a threshold slider, group-by slice dropdown, and an escalations tab where you set Slack pager channels.
[11:20] Aisha Khan: do you integrate with our change management? we have a deployment freeze windows sometimes.
[11:25] Priya Nair: yes, you can set deployment blackout windows and we will not auto-roll changes during those times; manual overrides are logged for audit.
[11:34] Carlos Mendez: how do historical drift visualizations look?
[11:38] Priya Nair: there's a time-series view per-metric showing deltas, with annotations for deployed prompt set changes; you can zoom to any date range and export.
[11:47] Tom Reeves: what's the underlying model catalog? can we pin exact model hashes?
[11:52] Priya Nair: yes each model version is stored with a fingerprint (commit-like hash) and runtime flags. you can pin to a model hash and we ensure the runtime uses that artifact until you change it.
[12:03] Aisha Khan: curious about large-scale runs — if we want to run evaluate across 1M samples, what's the recommended approach?
[12:10] Priya Nair: for big datasets we recommend sampling for CI-level quick checks and running full-batch offline runs in a Dedicated environment or using batch workers in your infra pointing to Redwood runtime images.
[12:23] Carlos Mendez: ok. mid-call note: are there demo limits we should be aware of when running our sample set?
[12:29] Priya Nair: ephemeral demo accounts have rate limits — but for pilot we lift them to realistic throughput.
[12:35] [12:37] Speaker 6: mention competitor comparison briefly
[12:39] Jordan Lee: just to call out — compared to Anthropic or OpenAI you get a more production-focused orchestration and native eval tooling; compared to Vertex AI we give easier routing and rollback semantics for live traffic.
[12:53] Carlos Mendez: any reference customers with retail use-case?
[12:56] Priya Nair: yes, Polaris Retail uses our eval pipeline for catalog mapping — happy to intro if that helps.
[13:05] Aisha Khan: that would be useful.
[13:08] [13:10] Jordan Lee: quick pause — want to open to Q&A on any technical nitty-gritty?
[13:16] Tom Reeves: yeah on the evaluation runner — what languages are the scoring hooks in? we use Python heavy stack.
[13:22] Priya Nair: Python and Node are supported out of the box; you can also run a containerized scorer for custom runtimes.
[13:30] Carlos Mendez: will the logs include input tokens masked for PII?
[13:35] Priya Nair: we support automatic redaction and policy-driven masking. you can define fields to mask and we will store a redacted transcript; raw unredacted is only accessible if you have KMS access and enable it.
[13:48] Aisha Khan: excellent. last question — how is billing structured for evaluation runs? flat rate or per-token?
[13:55] Jordan Lee: hosted evaluation is per-token plus a small per-run fee for heavy batch runs. Dedicated customers often include evaluation in their reserved capacity, reducing marginal costs.
[14:07] [14:10] Priya Nair: i want to highlight the 'quality gate' flow again — you define metrics, set thresholds, choose rollback policy and route rules. simulation mode lets you see what would have happened historically without changing live traffic.
[14:24] Tom Reeves: simulation mode would be ideal for our compliance team.
[14:28] Priya Nair: yep, it's built for that.
[14:31] Carlos Mendez: ok, i think we have enough to move forward. quick recap?
[14:35] Jordan Lee: recap: Redwood to share pilot pricing, security pack, SSO docs, and seed the evaluation baseline. Horizon to provide 1 week of sample queries, Okta contact, and confirm whether to pilot hosted (eu region) or spin up Dedicated. kickoff targeted 2026-11-09.
[14:55] Aisha Khan: sounds right.
[14:58] Tom Reeves: thanks — one quick ask, can Priya send the exact config JSON for the A/B we just ran? we want to include it in the ticket.
[15:05] Priya Nair: yes i'll attach the run config and the pairwise export.
[15:10] Jordan Lee: i'll drop the links in the follow-up thread and send the pilot quote by Thursday.
[15:17] [15:20] Carlos Mendez: great, appreciate it.
[15:22] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[15:25] [screen share ends]

Meeting end.
